part1_p1_contract_followed.deviation_note: The P1 spec named 'GET /api/ops/operators/<operator_id>/unified' as the illustrative route form; this pass implemented 'GET /api/ops/investigation/<address>/unified' instead (entity-address-keyed, not operator-id-keyed), because the primary reference case (Dv34) has NO operator_id -- it is a pre-candidate entity, not a canonical operator. Recorded explicitly per the instruction to document any deviation with reasoning; authority boundaries are unchanged (the route still reads operators.status via fetch_by_entity() exactly as designed).

part2_unified_read_projection.implementation: Three independent sqlite3 mode=ro connections (wt_ops_v2.db via fetch_by_entity, flex_complete_database.db for creator_funders historical count, local_operation_discovery_corpus.db for direct_funding_edges/candidate_families), each opened, queried, and closed separately. No ATTACH DATABASE statement. No cross-database write transaction of any kind.
part2_unified_read_projection.route: GET /api/ops/investigation/<address>/unified, added in src/ops/operator_routes.py (unified_investigation view function)

part3_authority_protection.principle_implemented: authority_state in the projection is populated ONLY via self.fetch_by_entity(entity_address)[0]['status'], which itself only ever SELECTs from operators/operator_entities. No code path in fetch_unified_investigation ever assigns authority_state from discovery, evidence_qualification, or funding_topology data.
part3_authority_protection.structural_proof: test_evidence_cannot_set_canonical_status_structural (greps the method body for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against 'operators' -- none found) and test_no_attach_database_cross_db_write_pattern in tests/test_ops_ui_p2_unified_implementation.py.
part3_authority_protection.candidate_role_never_becomes_authority: candidate_role is a SEPARATE dict key (identity.candidate_role) from authority_state; verified Dv34's authority_state=None while candidate_role=PROVISIONING_NETWORK_CANDIDATE simultaneously -- proves the two never collapse into one field.

part4_dv34_reference_result.method: Live call to OperatorReader(OPS_DB_PATH).fetch_unified_investigation('Dv34prGm2BT7Ph2n6qKLgzeLgjnii87RJJ7Db6ZQQvKM'), executed in this session, not hardcoded.

part4_dv34_reference_result.ui_never_shows_23_as_total: Confirmed both server-side (historical_population.count is a separate, always-populated field) and in the template change (the new panel always renders the historical count as the primary line; the HIGH-qualified figure only appears as an explicitly-labeled secondary breakdown, never replacing it).

part5_registry_card_enhancement.decision: NOT implemented on the bulk registry list (templates/operators_index.html) this pass -- the list already renders f.launches (historical population) as the primary count via the EXISTING familyRow()/rowHtml() functions, which was verified to already satisfy the 'never show 23 as total' requirement without any change. Adding a per-row secondary evidence-qualification line to the bulk list would require either (a) N additional HTTP requests per page load (one per row), violating Part 14/15's bounded-response requirement, or (b) embedding discovery-corpus data into the existing /api/ops/emerging-operators aggregate response, which is a larger, riskier change to a shared endpoint. Deferred as an explicit next step (see blockers).

part7_discovery_intake_into_analyst_queu.reasoning: Wiring 385-family discovery-corpus data into the existing Analyst Queue (rec.analyst_queue_reconciled in operators_index.html's load()) requires either extending /api/ops/emerging-operators (src/ops/emerging_operator_service.py, a large existing service) or adding a second merged fetch in the frontend load() function.
